title.narrative: Provision of life-saving, community-based preventive assistance to the most vulnerable populations in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas of Beletweyne District

description.narrative: ltpgtSOHHA will implement a community-based nutrition project in eight villages of Beletweyne District, focusing on vulnerable groups including children under five and PLW. The project aims to strengthen early detection and timely referral of acute malnutrition and improve IYCF practices. Protection principles will be integrated throughout to ensure services are delivered safely, respectfully, and inclusively. A four-day training will be conducted for 24 CHWs and IYCF counsellors on key IYCF topics including exclusive breastfeeding, complementary and responsive feeding, and behavior change communication strategies such as the “One Egg Per Child Per Day” campaign. Practical sessions will include culturally appropriate cooking demonstrations using nutrient-rich foods like Tom Brown porridge. A separate two-day training will cover micronutrient supplementation and deworming protocols, including management of deficiencies, distribution, monitoring, reporting, and community engagement. SOHHA will also train 4,000 caregivers and PLW on the Family MUAC approach to support early detection and referral at the household level. Additionally, three rounds of mass MUAC and oedema screening will target 7,600 individuals using KOBO Toolbox for real-time digital data collection.ltbrgtA four-day training for 16 CHWs and 8 IYCF counsellors will further strengthen capacity in screening and referral of acutely malnourished children and PLW, with a focus on practical MUAC use. This training will also integrate protection topics including Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention, child protection, and Prevention of Aid Diversion (PDAD). To enhance community engagement and sustainability, SOHHA will establish 48 care groups comprising 576 members (480 women and 96 men) to lead peer-driven social and behavior change communication (SBCC), organize household-level cooking demonstrations, and conduct culturally appropriate community dramas that promote nutrition and protection awareness. The project will support referrals for 144 children with complicated Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) to stabilization centers, 560 with uncomplicated SAM to outpatient therapeutic programs (OTPs), 2,160 with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) to targeted supplementary feeding programs (TSFPs), and 1,500 acutely malnourished PLW to TSFPs. Micronutrient interventions will include Vitamin A supplementation for 2,550 children under five, MNP distribution to 1,840 children and 896 PLW, and deworming of 2,050 children aged 12–59 months, all delivered through trained staff as part of routine outreach.ltbrgtMonitoring and reporting will be led by the Nutrition Officer, Project Manager, and MEAL team, with data collected by CHWs and IYCF counsellors using Somalia Nutrition Cluster-aligned tools disaggregated by age, gender, and disability. Community feedback will be gathered through hotlines, suggestion boxes, and quarterly dialogues. Real-time data collection using KOBO Toolbox will support evidence-based decision-making. Monthly monitoring and quarterly reviews will be based on referral forms, attendance sheets, and distribution logs. The project will deliver $40 vouchers to 810 vulnerable households, with vendor selection, contracting, targeting, distribution, and verification completed in the first three months. Coordination will occur through participation in national and sub-national Nutrition Cluster meetings, the area based coordination (ABC) group, and CVA Technical Working Group to ensure alignment and avoid duplication. The project’s exit strategy will emphasize sustainability and local ownership by building capacity among CHWs, counsellors, and care groups and integrating activities into local service platforms. Project closure will include joint reviews, lesson documentation, and handover to local actors to ensure long-term impact.ltbrgtlt/pgt
